The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages showed shoppers spend totals missing their latest purchases
Why, in plain words: The shop keeps saved copies of each shopper's running spend total, and these copies stopped being updated with new purchases for a reason the record does not show; account pages kept showing the out-of-date copies, likely because a page did not check a copy against the shopper's purchases before showing it.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 5m 55s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop - confirmed
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #528 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages showed shoppers spend totals missing their latest purchases
Incident: CachedSpendTotalsAreStale on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 02:07:30 UTC, not back to normal by 02:13:25 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 9 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 02:29:25 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:12:58 UTC
Ended by: Argus: discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop - confirmed, nothing to put back

Summary
The service broke at 02:07:30 UTC and was not back to normal by 02:13:25 UTC, at least 5 minutes 55 seconds later. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. The shop keeps saved copies of each shopper's running spend total, and these copies stopped being updated with new purchases for a reason the record does not show; account pages kept showing the out-of-date copies, likely because a page did not check a copy against the shopper's purchases before showing it. What Argus did: discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop - confirmed, nothing to put back. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #528, for a person to review and merge. Cached spend figures that were not on the discarded list, and any that went stale later, could keep showing shoppers totals that leave out their latest purchases, and more would go stale each time a shopper bought again.

Impact
at least 5m 55s - since onset, still not back to normal
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none so far - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: 90 of 240 cached spend figures disagree with the purchases behind them. The purchases are correct and the cached copies are behind: the widest gap is 89.29, the most any one figure is missing is 1 purchase, and the oldest purchase none of them account for was recorded at 2026-11-10T23:13:00Z, which is when the copies stopped keeping up, and they were being served from 2026-11-11T02:07:30Z. Discarding the entries listed will send those pages back to the purchase ledger, which never moved. The list is what disagreed when this check ran: nothing is putting the copies right, so a figure goes stale as soon as its shopper buys again and a later check will name more.

Root cause and contributing factors
The cached spend entries in io-summary-cache stopped taking in new purchases from Nov 10, 23:13 UTC, so they fell behind the purchase ledger, which stayed correct. The evidence read does not show why the updates stopped.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that left out purchases they had made. The purchases themselves were recorded correctly.
  Evidence:
    AL1
why 1 The pages were serving cached copies of the spend figures from io-summary-cache that had fallen behind the purchase ledger, while the ledger itself stayed correct. These stale cached copies were the whole of what was wrong.
  Evidence:
    AL1
    T20 02:13:25 Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - discarded 90 of io-shop's stale cached figures and the store reported what it removed, which is the whole of what was wrong
why 2 The cached copies stopped taking in new purchases from Nov 10, 23:13 UTC. The oldest purchase that no stale figure counted was recorded then. What stopped the updates is not shown: the Investigator Agent got back no metrics and no log lines for the service.
  Evidence:
    AL1
    T4 02:13:13 Investigator Agent: Read back 0 minutes of metrics
    T10 02:13:15 Investigator Agent: Read back 0 log lines
    T12 02:13:16 Investigator Agent: Read back 0 log lines
  Ruled out:
    A deploy, release or flag change on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 5 minutes 24 seconds before Nov 11 02:12:54; the Investigator Agent read back 0 production changes.
      T7
      T8
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:13:17.
      T16
Contributing factors
- Code-Fix read src/io_shop/account_page.py, and nothing ran that reading. In it, the account page's `_the_figure_for` serves any entry the cache returns without comparing the entry's purchase count with the purchases the page has already loaded for that account. So a stale entry kept being served for as long as the cache could be reached. (AI-2)
- Nothing was seen watching whether io-summary-cache's updates kept up with the purchase ledger. The copies stopped keeping up at Nov 10, 23:13 UTC, and the only thing that found it was the stale-figure check, once stale figures were being served. (AI-6)
- The CachedSpendTotalsAreStale alert was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged. (AI-7)
- No per-minute metrics and no log lines came back for the service when the Investigator Agent asked for them. (AI-8, AI-9)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The cached spend totals (io-summary-cache) stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger from Nov 10, 2026, 23:13 UTC and began being served stale at 02:07:30 UTC. The ledger is correct and only the derived copy is behind. No deploy, flag or placement change was recorded. | 0.70 | confirmed
C2 | The internal io-summary-cache service, owned by checkout-platform, failed to apply updates and so served stale totals. | 0.15 | confirmed, as tested for C1

Trigger
C1 was confirmed, but Argus could not tie io-summary-cache to any change it read.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:13:23 | Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop for C1 | Argus | nothing to put back | confirmed
 | 02:15:02 | Proposed a fix: PR #528 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 02:07:30 UTC. CachedSpendTotalsAreStale fired at 02:12:54 UTC, 5 minutes 24 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #528 | open
AI-3 | Restore io-summary-cache's updates so cached spend figures take in new purchases again. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Until the cache's updates are restored, re-run the stale-figure check and discard the entries it names. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Find out what stopped io-summary-cache from taking in new purchases from Nov 10, 23:13 UTC, including any change made to io-summary-cache itself. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Add an alert that fires when io-summary-cache's updates fall behind the purchase ledger, whether or not stale entries are being served yet. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Route CachedSpendTotalsAreStale to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-8 | Make io-shop's per-minute metrics readable to the Investigator Agent. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-9 | Make io-shop's log lines readable to the Investigator Agent, or find out why none came back for the hours before the alert. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert named each stale entry and pointed to a safe fallback: the purchase ledger, which never moved. That made it clear what to discard.
- 23 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:13:17.
- 29 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent discarded the stale cached figures of io-shop for C1.
- 31 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 2 minutes 8 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #528.
What went wrong
- The mitigation discarded only the entries that disagreed when the alert's check ran. Nothing seen restarted the cache's updates, so the copies were left free to go stale again.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Response effort
none - engineer time
154,784 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/15fd807b-1dcf-4fdb-8d5b-38b47692b88b
The fix it proposed: PR #528 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/528) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
Read; none came back.
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: in src/io_shop/account_page.py, _the_figure_for returned found.amount_cents for any entry cached_summary handed back. It never compared the entry with the account it was rendering. An entry that stopped being updated went on being served as long as the cache could be reached, so the page had no defence against a cache that fell behind the ledger. Nothing was deployed and no flag changed: the cache's feed just stopped keeping up, and every page read whatever the cache still held.

The data to catch this was already there. A SummaryEntry (src/io_shop/summary_cache.py) holds items_counted, the number of purchases the figure was worked out over. The page already has account.purchases loaded, and src/io_shop/cache_reconciliation.py uses that same comparison (len(account.purchases) - entry.items_counted) to report stale entries. The page now runs the check before serving: an entry is used only when items_counted == len(account.purchases). Anything else is treated like a miss, so the page works the figure out from the purchases (the same fallback it already uses for a miss or an unreachable cache), reports served_from_cache=False, and the share of recomputed pages shows the drift. The cache stays optional, CacheUnreachable handling is unchanged, and pages without a cache configured are untouched.

Tests (tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py): a_cache_holding now takes the purchase count. The existing cached-figure test builds an entry that matches the account's two purchases. Before, it used a hard-coded count of 8, which only passed because the count was never checked. A new test builds an entry counting one purchase for an account with two. It asserts the page shows the computed figure (2000), not the cached one, and reports served_from_cache as False. Against the current code that test would get 999 and True.

Limit: this catches entries that missed purchases or count extra ones. It would not catch an entry with the right count but a wrong amount. That isn't the stale-copy pattern the investigation describes.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
○ Key incident data collected (for a person)
  no minute of metrics came back for the incident window; collecting them is for a person
○ Impact assessed (for a person)
  the loss is measured to the close; when the service is back to normal is for a person to report
✗ Root-cause analysis complete (not met)
  the chain does not reach a cause
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For at least {duration}, account pages on io-shop showed some shoppers a spend total that left out their latest purchases. The shop keeps saved copies of each shopper's running spend total. These copies stopped being updated with new purchases, and the record does not show why. Account pages kept showing the out-of-date copies, likely because a page did not check a copy against the shopper's purchases before showing it. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, so no on-call responder was called in. Argus threw away the out-of-date saved figures, and it has confirmed that this step worked. Argus also wrote a proposed fix, which is still a draft and has not been put into use.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
